newsitem.title: USA: Kohl says number of EMU participants "sufficient".
newsitem.headline: Kohl says number of EMU participants "sufficient".

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Tuesday that a sufficient number of countries will meet the criteria mandated for participation in the planned European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

"I cannot tell you who will participate, even if I knew, I would not tell you because that would not be right. But there will be a sufficient number of countries (meeting) the criteria," Kohl said in a speech sponsored by the German American Chamber of Commerce Inc.
Kohl was speaking in German, and an English-language translation was provided by the Chamber of Commerce.
Kohl stressed that Europe's planned single currency, to be called the euro, will be launched and that the timetable is clear.
"I want to make one thing very clear in this house...that is, that the euro will be introduced," Kohl said.
"There is very clear wording in the (Maastricht) treaty. The criteria are clear; the timetable is clear," he added.
Europe's proposed single currency is scheduled to be launched on January 1, 1999.
In his speech, Kohl made no specific reference to this date, or the names of possible nation participants in EMU.
